question: In your vehicle, what should you adjust before you start your engine?
handbookAnswer: Adjust the seat to reach all controls and adjust all mirrors (also: park/neutral, clear the view, lock doors, buckle up)

question: What are the equipment requirements for windshields and side windows?
handbookAnswer: Windshield: safety glass, not reflective or non-transparent, no stickers not required by law; side windows may not reflect more than 25% of light, rear window 35%

question: What are bumper height requirements? Are they the same for every vehicle?
handbookAnswer: Maximum bumper heights depend on the vehicle's net shipping weight (not modified weight), so they differ by vehicle (e.g. cars < 2,500 lbs: 22 in. front and rear)

question: What must you do if hauling a load of material which could fall or blow onto the roadway?
handbookAnswer: Use a close-fitting cover; the load must not drop, shift, leak or escape

question: When a projected load extends more than 4 feet from the vehicle, what must you use to clearly mark it in the daytime? At night?
handbookAnswer: Day: red flags at least 18 in. square at the load's extremities; night/rain/smoke/fog: two red lamps visible 500 ft to the rear, red reflectors, side lamps

question: Why is drowsy driving dangerous?
handbookAnswer: Fatigue slows thinking and reaction, affects judgment and vision, can cause micro-sleep; as dangerous as drunk driving

question: What should you do if another driver is threatening you or intentionally driving dangerously around you?
handbookAnswer: Stay calm, put distance between you, slow down and let them pass, no eye contact or gestures; call *FHP (*347) or 911

question: What are the three main categories of distracted driving?
handbookAnswer: Visual, manual and cognitive

question: Why is texting one of the most dangerous of distracted driving behaviors?
handbookAnswer: Texting involves all three kinds of distraction

question: Can anyone drink and drive safely?
handbookAnswer: No; even one drink affects driving

question: Both your judgment and vision are affected after drinking alcohol. Which is affected first?
handbookAnswer: Judgment is affected first

question: What can happen to you if you are in a crash and not wearing a seat belt?
handbookAnswer: You are far more likely to be killed: ejected, thrown against others/wheel/windshield, lose control

question: What age are children required to be in a car seat? In a car seat or booster seat?
handbookAnswer: Under 4: child safety seat; ages 4-5: safety seat or booster seat

question: If a law enforcement officer stops a vehicle and a front seat passenger (under 18 years old) is not wearing a safety belt, who will be charged with the seat belt violation?
handbookAnswer: The driver

question: What does a single broken white line on the highway mean?
handbookAnswer: Lanes in the same direction; you may cross it to change lanes when safe

question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of the highway mean? A double solid white line?
handbookAnswer: Double solid yellow: no passing/crossing either direction (left turns and passing a bicyclist allowed when safe); double solid white: no lane changes across it

question: What does a solid yellow line to the right of the center line of the highway mean?
handbookAnswer: Solid line on your side of the center line: no passing from your lane

question: What do the colors of traffic signs indicate (red, orange, yellow, etc.)?
handbookAnswer: Red stop/prohibition, orange construction, yellow warning, fluorescent yellow-green school/ped/bike, white regulatory, green guide, blue services, brown recreation

question: When more than one vehicle approaches a four-way stop sign, which one moves first?
handbookAnswer: First to arrive goes first; at the same time, yield to the driver on the right

question: What does a red traffic light mean? What does a flashing red traffic light mean?
handbookAnswer: Red: stop and stay stopped; flashing red: stop, then go when safe

question: After a full stop at a red traffic light when may a driver turn right?
handbookAnswer: After a full stop, if no NO TURN ON RED sign and the way is clear

question: What does a green arrow showing at the same time as a red traffic light mean you can do?
handbookAnswer: You may turn in the arrow's direction (from the proper lane), yielding to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection

question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
handbookAnswer: Proceed with caution

question: If you are approaching a railroad crossing that does not have gates or lights and you see a train coming, what should you do?
handbookAnswer: Stop: a visible approaching train requires a stop; crossbucks mean yield to trains

question: What happens to the force of impact when you double your speed? Triple your speed?
handbookAnswer: Doubling speed makes impact (and braking distance) 4 times greater; tripling makes it 9 times greater

question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit for cars in a residential area?
handbookAnswer: 30 MPH

question: What is the maximum speed limit on an interstate highway?
handbookAnswer: 70 MPH

question: Can you be issued a ticket for driving too slowly?
handbookAnswer: Yes; driving so slowly that you block or delay normal traffic is illegal (minimum 50 MPH where the limit is 70)

question: What are the steps for making a smooth stop?
handbookAnswer: Check mirrors and blind spots, release the accelerator, brake with steady pressure

question: What is the arm signal for a left turn? Right turn? Slow or stop?
handbookAnswer: Left: arm straight out; right: arm bent up; slow/stop: arm bent down

question: How long (distance) should you signal before making a left or right turn?
handbookAnswer: At least 100 feet

question: When can you use a three-point turn? Where should you never make a three-point turn?
handbookAnswer: Only when the road is too narrow for a U-turn and you can't go around the block; never on a curve, hill or highway or where U-turns are prohibited

question: What is an open intersection? When must you yield right-of-way?
handbookAnswer: No signs or signals; yield if a vehicle is already in it, if entering/crossing a state highway from a secondary road, if entering a paved road from an unpaved road, or if turning left across oncoming traffic

question: When may you drive in the left lane of a road with two lanes? With four lanes?
handbookAnswer: Two-lane: drive in the right lane except to pass; four or more lanes: keep to the right lanes except to pass

question: What does it mean if you see red reflectors on the lane lines facing you? What should you do?
handbookAnswer: You are on the wrong side of the road (or wrong way on a ramp); get into the proper lane or turn around immediately

question: What is the recommended safe following distance?
handbookAnswer: At least 4 seconds

question: When should you increase your following distance?
handbookAnswer: Increase it in rain or low visibility, when being passed, when towing or carrying heavy loads, and behind motorcycles and some other vehicles

question: What are blind spots?
handbookAnswer: Areas near the rear corners you can't see in your mirrors

question: How do you check your blind spots when you are preparing to change lanes or turn?
handbookAnswer: Turn your head and look

question: Where is it unlawful to overtake and pass?
handbookAnswer: Solid lines, no-passing zones, hills/curves without 500 ft of sight, within 100 ft of intersections/bridges/tunnels/railroad crossings, stopped school bus, crosswalk with a stopped car

question: Under what circumstances can you stop in the acceleration lane on an expressway?
handbookAnswer: Only if traffic is too heavy and there is no space to enter safely

question: What should you do if you drive past your exit on an interstate highway?
handbookAnswer: Go on to the next exit

question: Where should you move your vehicle if you break down while driving on the highway?
handbookAnswer: Completely off the pavement (no more than 6 hours on a limited access highway)

question: What is the farthest away you can park from a curb?
handbookAnswer: 12 inches

question: If you have a manual transmission, what gear should you put the car in when parking downhill? Uphill? What if you have an automatic transmission?
handbookAnswer: Manual: reverse downhill, first uphill; automatic: park

question: Where is parking prohibited?
handbookAnswer: Crosswalks, sidewalks, bike lanes, intersections, bridges, tunnels, driveways, yellow curbs, double parking, within 15/20/30/50 ft limits, etc.

question: Which way should you turn your wheels when parking uphill along a curb? Which way should you turn them where there is not a curb? Which way should you turn them if parking downhill?
handbookAnswer: Uphill with curb: away from the curb; uphill without curb: to the right; Downhill: toward the curb

question: Are motorists required to stop or yield for pedestrians crossing the street?
handbookAnswer: Yes, stop and stay stopped for pedestrians crossing at any marked crossing or intersection

question: What must you do when you see a pedestrian with a white cane in the street ahead of you?
handbookAnswer: Stop and let the pedestrian cross

question: What is the minimum distance a motorist must give when traveling next to a cyclist?
handbookAnswer: 3 feet

question: As a motorist, what should you do when preparing to turn right on a roadway with a bike lane?
handbookAnswer: Yield to bicyclists and turn behind them

question: When on the roadway, do motorcyclists and moped riders have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers?
handbookAnswer: Yes, the same rights and duties; riders can be cited

question: If you are driving a motor vehicle, are you allowed to share a lane with a motorcyclist?
handbookAnswer: No; a motorcyclist is entitled to the full lane

question: When a school bus is stopped to unload children on a highway divided with a raised barrier, are vehicles traveling in the opposite direction required to stop?
handbookAnswer: No (raised barrier or unpaved median at least 5 ft); proceed with caution

question: When a school bus stops to unload children, are vehicles traveling in the same direction required to stop?
handbookAnswer: Yes, always

question: What must you do when children or school crossing guards are present in a crosswalk?
handbookAnswer: Yield and stop at the stop line, not in the crosswalk

question: What must you do if an emergency vehicle with activated lights and/or sirens is approaching you from behind?
handbookAnswer: Pull over to the closest edge of the road and stop until it passes

question: What does the Move Over law require you to do?
handbookAnswer: Vacate the lane next to the stopped vehicle or slow to 20 MPH below the limit (5 MPH if the limit is 20 or less)

question: What is a “No Zone”?
handbookAnswer: Blind spots around trucks and buses

question: At what times must you use your headlights?
handbookAnswer: Sunset to sunrise and in rain, smoke or fog

question: At night, within how many feet of approaching a vehicle from the rear must you dim your bright headlights?
handbookAnswer: 300 feet

question: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle should you dim your bright headlights?
handbookAnswer: 500 feet

question: When driving in the rain, fog, or smoke in the daytime, what lights should you use?
handbookAnswer: Headlights on low beam

question: What should you do when driving on wet roads in the rain? Why?
handbookAnswer: Slow down and increase following distance: roads are slick (oil), stopping takes longer, hydroplaning risk

question: What should you do if your right wheels go off the pavement while driving?
handbookAnswer: Ease off the gas, hold the wheel firmly, brake lightly, return slowly when clear

question: What should you do if your tires begin to skid while driving?
handbookAnswer: Foot off the gas, avoid braking, steer where you want to go

question: When emergency braking, what is the difference between conventional brakes and anti-lock brakes (ABS)?
handbookAnswer: Conventional brakes: pump them; ABS: press hard, hold and steer (pumping disengages ABS)

question: What should you do during a tire blow-out?
handbookAnswer: Foot off the gas, don't brake, steer, slow gradually, brake softly once under control, pull off

question: What must you do if you are involved in a minor accident and your vehicle is blocking the flow of traffic?
handbookAnswer: Move the vehicle (or have it moved) out of traffic

question: If you hit a parked car and are unable to find the owner, what should you do?
handbookAnswer: Leave a note with your name, contact information and plate number; notify law enforcement

question: What are the penalties for leaving the scene of an accident involving injury or death?
handbookAnswer: Death: first-degree felony, minimum 4 years prison; serious bodily injury: second-degree felony; injury: third-degree felony; all with at least 3 years' license loss

question: What are the requirements of the No-Fault law?
handbookAnswer: Proof of $10,000 PIP and $10,000 PDL from a Florida-licensed insurer, kept continuously

question: If your license and registration are suspended for being in violation of the No-Fault law, what must you do to get them reinstated?
handbookAnswer: Get insurance and pay a $150-$500 reinstatement fee; no temporary license for any reason

question: What are the penalties if you are at fault in a crash and you are not insured in compliance with the Financial Responsibility Law?
handbookAnswer: Prove financial responsibility; FLHSMV can require you to pay the damages before reinstatement; license/plates suspended up to 3 years without required higher coverage

question: What are the time restrictions for a driver with a learner’s license?
handbookAnswer: Learner: daylight only for 3 months, then until 10 p.m., with a licensed driver 21+

question: What are the time restrictions for a licensed driver under age 17? Under age 18?
handbookAnswer: Age 16: not 11 p.m.-6 a.m.; age 17: not 1-5 a.m. (unless to/from work or with a licensed driver 21+)

question: When can you be charged with driving under the influence (DUI)?
handbookAnswer: Driving or in physical control while under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances, prescription or over-the-counter drugs; administrative suspension at .08+ BAL

question: What are the penalties for refusing to take a blood test, a urine test, or a breath test when suspected of driving under the influence?
handbookAnswer: First refusal: 1-year suspension; second: 18 months and a first-degree misdemeanor

question: What can happen if you are found guilty of racing on the highway?
handbookAnswer: License revocation (racing is on the revocation list) and a required basic driver improvement course

question: If you have a learner’s license, how many hours of driving experience are required to earn the Class E license?
handbookAnswer: 50 hours, including 10 at night

question: What education course are you required to take if you are applying for a learner’s license (or have never held a driver’s license)?
handbookAnswer: Traffic Law and Substance Abuse Education (TLSAE)

question: Are you required to notify DHSMV of any health problems that may affect your driving?
handbookAnswer: Yes: list physical or mental conditions on the application; a doctor's medical report may be required

question: Why would one opt to take a Basic Driver Improvement Course?
handbookAnswer: To avoid points for a noncriminal moving violation (18% off the civil penalty; not if >30 MPH over); possible insurance discount

question: What maneuvers are required on a driving skills test?
handbookAnswer: Approach of crossing, backing 50 ft looking back (no mirror/camera), following distance, stop signs, signals, right-of-way, parking on a grade, passing, signal and turn, proper lane, quick stop, straight-in parking, three-point turn in 20-40 ft
